summary: This section explains how a company decides the pay for its managers when the company has little or no profit. Even with other rules in this chapter, the company can set this pay within the limits allowed by the law. When deciding the amount, the company must look at certain specific factors like the person's qualifications and the company's financial health.
points: Applies when a company approves an appointment or pay under sections 196 or 197 and has inadequate or no profits.
Allows the company to fix the pay as a specific amount or a percentage of profits within the limits of the Act.
Requires the company to consider its own financial position when fixing the pay.
Requires the company to consider any other pay or commission the person gets in other capacities or from other companies.
Requires the company to consider the professional qualifications and experience of the individual.
example: Meera Textiles Private Limited has no profits this year, but the company wants to appoint a new managing director under section 196. As allowed by the law, the company decides to fix the remuneration within the permitted limits. Before finalizing the amount, the board of directors reviews the company's weak financial position and checks the professional qualifications and long experience of the candidate. They also look at the commission the candidate draws from another company. After considering all these required factors, Meera Textiles Private Limited fixes a fair remuneration amount as deemed fit.

terms.meaning: Money or payment given to a person for work or services.
A situation where a business earns very little money or makes no profit at all.

watch: Do not assume this section allows unlimited pay when profits are low; the amount must still stay within the limits specified by the Act.
